cadence: Curated weekly; citation rankings still refresh every Monday.
selection: Official model, harness, and research announcements selected for recency, AI4AI relevance, technical novelty, and source verifiability. Performance claims remain attributed to their publishers.

items.title: GLM-5.3: Frontier Coding with Emergent Cyber Capabilities
items.why: Z.ai says the unchanged GLM-5.2 base gained stronger long-horizon coding and cyber capabilities entirely through scaled post-training; weights are planned after two weeks of safety hardening.

items.title: dots3-note Preview
items.why: The first open-weight Dots3 release is a multimodal MoE with 280B total and 16B active parameters, a 512K context window, and explicit support for long-horizon agent tasks.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.why: Google positions 3.7 Flash as its coding-and-agents workhorse, reporting stronger multi-step planning, tool use, software engineering, and business-workflow performance.

items.title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro GA Release
items.why: DeepSeek's general-availability release emphasizes agent upgrades, low/high/max reasoning effort, native OpenAI Responses API support, and availability across its app, web interface, and API.

items.title: voyage-code-4: Code Retrieval Built for Coding Agents
items.why: Voyage AI's new code-embedding model targets repository retrieval for coding agents, with configurable dimensions and quantization options intended to reduce retrieval cost.

items.title: Introducing NAC, an Open-Source Harness for Long-Running Agent Work
items.why: NAC is an Apache-2.0 agent harness for durable long-running execution, presenting the harness as an inference runtime rather than a fixed prompt-and-tool wrapper.

items.title: Introducing Grok 4.6
items.why: Grok 4.6 targets long-running agents and multi-step coding and knowledge work; xAI reports stronger sustained execution, self-testing, and verification after supplemental training and agentic RL.

items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard
items.why: NVIDIA pairs an efficient model for long-running agent workloads with an open-source router that selects models per workflow step according to quality, latency, and cost.

items.title: ALTK-Evolve: Learning from Agent Trajectories with Fewer Tokens
items.why: ALTK-Evolve extracts, consolidates, and retrieves reusable lessons from agent trajectories without weight updates; IBM reports similar or better accuracy than ACE with lower token use.

items.title: Introducing Muse Glimmer: An Open Agentic Model That Runs on Your Device
items.why: Meta's 30B open-weight multimodal model is tuned for sequential tool use and local always-on agents, with an Apache-2.0 release and deployment paths for personal hardware.
